req.title: Pagination via skip and limit
req.statement: The system shall skip the first 'skip' items and cap the returned count at 'limit' when both are supplied to GET /tasks/.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /tasks/?skip=<s>&limit=<l> skips the first s items and returns at most l items. The pre-loaded dataset has exactly 20 rows (ids 1-20). Tests cover: (1) EP positive — typical skip+limit returning a deterministic slice; (2) EP positive — skip+limit together isolate a mid-range window; (3) BVA boundary — limit=1 (minimum allowed) returns exactly one item; (4) BVA boundary — skip equal to total row count returns empty list; (5) BVA boundary — limit at maximum allowed value (1000) returns all 20 rows; (6) NEG — skip=-1 triggers 422; (7) NEG — limit=0 triggers 422 (ge=1 constraint); (8) DT — skip=0,limit=20 returns all 20 rows exactly; (9) BVA — skip=19 (last item) returns exactly 1 row; (10) BVA — limit=100 (default cap constant) with 20 rows returns all 20. Each test asserts exact status codes, exact list lengths, and exact id values where deterministic, killing off-by-one, operator-flip, and constant-bump mutations.

tests.name: test_skip_and_limit_typical_window
actions: Inspect response status code and body
expected: Response body is a list of exactly 3 tasks
First returned task has id=3 (rows 3,4,5 after skipping 1,2)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_skip_and_limit_typical_window():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/?skip=2&limit=3")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.json()
    assert isinstance(data, list)
    assert len(data) == 3
    ids = [item["id"] for item in data]
    assert ids == [3, 4, 5]

test_skip_and_limit_typical_window()

preconditions: Task schema exposes id, title, description, completed, created_at, updated_at
actions: Inspect all fields of the single returned task
expected: Returned task has id=1, title='Read chapter 5', completed=true
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_skip_and_limit_exact_payload_fields():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/?skip=0&limit=1")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.json()
    assert len(data) == 1
    task = data[0]
    assert task["id"] == 1
    assert task["title"] == "Read chapter 5"
    assert task["completed"] is True
    assert "created_at" in task
    assert "description" in task

test_skip_and_limit_exact_payload_fields()
